subject: geese
one_liner: A battle royale for geese. Six birds enter a public park; one leaves claiming the drain.
brand_voice_notes: Park-sign directness. Territorial entitlement, extravagant construction and conspicuous plumage. Plain controls; jokes in the consequences. No specialist knowledge required.

hero.h1: The park is public. The chip is yours.
hero.sub: Gander is a battle royale for geese. Grab the picnic chip, build a lookout and follow the shrinking safe zone. The final territory is a drain. You will defend it anyway.

features.title: Build yourself out of lunch.
features.blurb: Stack three ramps for the best view in the park. From up there, you can watch Dennis eat the chip you were guarding.

features.title: Dress to be found.
features.blurb: Swap gray feathers for gold. The shrub still hides a goose, but it now appears to be hiding a small chandelier.

features.title: Win less ground. More personally.
features.blurb: Each storm circle pushes the flock closer to the drain. By the final round, six acres of disputed park have become one very important hole.

demo_screen_concept: One interactive top-down public-park match with six geese remaining. Adjacent-patch movement, three timber ramps, gray/gold outfit selection, storm circles converging on the drain, a next-circle minimap, health, materials, remaining-player count, four squad slots, a plain-language event log and deterministic reset. Three ramps put Arthur above his chip as Dennis eats it below. Gold visibly glints and changes Hidden to Spotted.

observations.consequence: The player builds a grand lookout and loses the chip directly beneath it.

observations.behavior: Wanting every rival to admire your appearance.
observations.consequence: Gold attracts the attention the hiding goose was trying to avoid.

observations.behavior: Refusing to back down from a trivial territorial dispute.
observations.mechanic: Shrinking storm circles and last-bird-standing resolution.
observations.consequence: Winning the park means defending a drain nobody wanted at the start.

references.reference: Peterson Field Guide bird identification plates
references.cues: Clear goose silhouettes, side-profile studies, restrained natural colors and small arrows identifying visible differences.
references.application: Use original illustrated goose studies for the outfit comparison. An arrow points to the gold feather glint as a practical identification detail. Keep species-style captions readable and outside the artwork; reproduce no existing plates or branding.

references.reference: Municipal pond-side 'Do not feed the birds' signs and park wayfinding maps
references.cues: Sturdy slab lettering, dark olive sign panels, pale backgrounds, simplified paths and direct instructions.
references.application: Use the signage hierarchy for headlines and section markers, and park-map geometry for the playable arena. Actual controls use plain labels such as Move, Build ramp and Next circle. Create original symbols and notices without municipal seals.

audience_design.landing_application: Pond-side municipal signs meet illustrated bird identification plates: reed olive, pale sky and chalk; Lora bold naturalist headings with Raleway functional text; broad asymmetric opening and rounded pond-map geometry. The playable preview precedes large artwork. Open text passages and generous gutters avoid repeating a card grid.
audience_design.demo_application: Keep the battle-royale arena central with HUD, next-circle inset, four squad slots, outfit strip and material-limited construction. Field-guide goose pieces inhabit a six-by-six park map with visible paths, pond, bins, chip and drain. At mobile widths the controls stack after the full-width board; all actions have keyboard-operable buttons.

design_direction.style: Illustrated park-wayfinding: sturdy naturalist type, broad sky fields, olive signage and contour-shaped pond boundaries. A field guide with an active territorial dispute.

palette.name: Pond Sky, Reed Olive and Chalk

fonts.pairing: Wellness Calm from bundled ui-ux-pro-max library, given heavier field-guide headings

design_direction.archetype: Product Demo + Features from bundled landing library; proposition and recognizable match preview, three behavior-led features, two explanatory art spreads, player evidence, cosmetic purchase comparison.
design_direction.motion_vocab: 160ms button color changes; user-triggered map changes only. No ambient movement. Reduced motion disables transitions.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Wide asymmetrical sky opening, short large heading beside a park arena preview. A chalk rules band leads to construction art and outfit identification art. Pricing resembles three reserve admission options. Demo uses the same kit with compact functional density.
design_direction.design_review: Compared seven entries dated November 5–11, excluding this recovery and other November 12 experiments. No matching style/palette/font tuple. This entry uses natural-history illustration and park contours instead of sports video, huddles, seed cells, parcels, tickets or film stills. Rejected automatic claymorphism/newsletter recommendation because it does not serve the approved game workflow.

brand_kit.identity_rationale: A goose neck combined with territorial contour lines gives a municipal bird warning its own identity. Slab wordmark, natural-history gouache and rounded pond contours express public-park entitlement. Differs from the recent lifting strap, speech huddle, seed selection and parcel identities.

images.rationale: Recovery reuses the existing Gemini-designed logo family, two composed graphics and specimen-derived game pieces. Zero new image generations. Original prompts, attempts and rejected records below are preserved from the prior entry; they are historical provenance, not new calls. Functional map and controls are native HTML/CSS.

items.prompt: Design the actual finished original identity for "Gander", a battle royale for geese who claim public parks. Direction A: a bold compact goose-neck silhouette integrated with two irregular territory contour lines, beside bespoke sturdy slab-serif wordmark spelling exactly "Gander". Give the symbol a distinctive poised hostile goose character, legible without tiny details. Municipal pond-side bird warning meets naturalist field guide. Flat reed olive #4D572A on plain chalk #F4F1E5, tiny rust #B94F32 accent permitted. Horizontal lockup, symbol left in left quarter, lettering right. Generous clear space. No tagline, no mockup, no presentation board, no frames, no gradients, no source game trademarks. This is final usable logo artwork, not a concept sheet. Crisp edges, sophisticated optical spacing. Only text: Gander.
items.verdict: Accepted direction A: correct Gander spelling, distinct goose/contour symbol, readable at 200px navigation and recognizable at 32px icon. Stronger separate symbol and mixed-case readability than B.

items.prompt: Revise the attached Gander editorial campaign artwork. First attached image is APPROVED IDENTITY REFERENCE. Second attached image is EDIT TARGET. Preserve its successful original gouache style, palette, large headline "A better view of losing your chip.", contour-lined ground, picnic scene and typographic hierarchy. Fix the central story: put the vigilant gray goose on the HIGHEST lookout platform at the upper right, fully visible. Remove the goose from the low left platform so there are exactly TWO geese in the whole image: one at the very top looking down, one on the ground eating the stolen french fry. There must be exactly THREE rising wooden ramps in a clear zigzag route up to the highest platform; no extra descending stairs. Use the label "3 ramps" ONLY ONCE near the structure. Use "1 chip" ONLY ONCE beside the eating goose, and show only one chip in its beak. Retain the exact Gander logo at bottom right faithfully. No extra text, no repeated labels, no new words. All essential details and words must remain within margins. This is the final finished campaign illustration, not a mockup.
items.verdict: Accepted corrected composition: goose now at highest platform, single 3 ramps label, rival eating at ground level. Headline correctly spelled and large. Fine stair detail is illustrative; live text carries the exact mechanic.
items.recovery_review: Reused existing local asset; original generation provenance retained. No new generation in this recovery.

items.prompt: Create a finished natural-history identification infographic for Gander. Attached logo is APPROVED IDENTITY REFERENCE; use its slab typography, goose silhouette character and olive contour language. An original two-column Peterson-inspired bird field-guide study, not copied from any existing illustration. Exact headline "Same shrub. Different odds." Across two equal-sized circular shrub cutaways, place a realistic gouache Canada goose of equal scale, one wearing standard gray feathers almost blending into olive foliage, the other with metallic GOLD feathers visibly glinting through the equivalent shrub. Both birds must be easy to find for the viewer while gray is clearly subtler. Use carefully drawn nested map-contour sightlines around each bush, gold side with multiple rust sightline ticks and a conspicuous bright reflective starburst that is a physical sun reflection, not decorative branding. Label left "Gray" and beneath "Hidden"; label right "Gold" and beneath "Spotted". Add small exact bottom line "Appearance changes. Cover does not." These are all the words; no gibberish or extra text. A composed data-story plate with editorial hierarchy, paired illustrations, clear large labels, generous breathing room. Background chalk #F4F1E5, reed olive #4D572A, pale sky #DCE7EA, rust #B94F32 and gold #C8A339 only. Fine print grain, museum-quality hand-painted bird studies. Landscape 3:2, large mobile-readable typography, no UI, photographs or watermarks.
items.placement: Landing outfit passage and demo field guide
items.verdict: Accepted: equal-scale paired geese, clear Gray/Hidden and Gold/Spotted labels, visible reflection. Readable primary hierarchy at 360px; fine bottom line repeated in live HTML.
items.recovery_review: Reused existing local asset; original generation provenance retained. No new generation in this recovery.

items.prompt: Create two isolated original natural-history gouache Canada goose full-body profile illustrations for Gander park-map game pieces, using attached image as APPROVED IDENTITY AND STYLE REFERENCE. Exactly TWO geese separated widely, left half standard gray Canada goose, right half same shape goose with reflective gold plumage, black neck and white cheek retained in both. Both face right, standing on feet, full body including head and tail, same scale. Detailed feather planes but strong clear silhouette, alert territorially offended posture, dry wit, field-guide specimen treatment. Reed olive #4D572A, neutral gray, gold #C8A339, beak dark. Absolutely uniform pure white background #FFFFFF for faithful deterministic background removal, NO shadows, NO scenery, NO letters, NO labels, NO logo, NO UI, NO text. Two specimens centered in separate left and right halves with ample margins, never overlapping. Landscape 3:2.
items.verdict: Accepted: consistent gray and gold Canada geese, clean silhouettes, no text; same alert posture.

Direction B: a bespoke chunky slab-serif Gander wordmark with a sculptural goose neck and head emerging from its capital G, the lower G suggesting a drain grille. Restrained original municipal park-sign identity. Flat reed olive #4D572A and rust #B94F32 on plain chalk #F4F1E5. No separate generic badge. discarded.verdict: Rejected direction B: heavier uppercase silhouette, less independently usable symbol and more awkward goose/G join.

discarded.prompt: Create a finished sophisticated editorial graphic for Gander, the goose battle royale. Attached image is the APPROVED IDENTITY REFERENCE: preserve its goose silhouette attitude, olive contour motif, slab-serif lettering and palette. Not a logo sheet. Compose a landscape illustrated park field study: on the left a gray Canada goose stands VERY HIGH on an elaborate timber structure of exactly THREE ascending ramps plus top lookout platform; at ground level below, a second Canada goose casually eats a single french fry beside a picnic blanket. The effort-versus-reward joke must read instantly. Original natural-history gouache with rich feather detail, flat municipal sign typography, pale sky #DCE7EA, chalk #F4F1E5, reed olive #4D572A, timber neutral brown, rust #B94F32 accents. Controlled paper grain. Editorial design with confident negative space and clear depth, slim contour-line ground pattern. Integrate large readable exact headline "A better view of losing your chip." at upper left and deliberate labels "3 ramps" next to the tall structure and "1 chip" next to the eating goose. No UI mockup, photo, generic shapes, checkerboard or watermarks. Wide 3:2 composition, keep all key text away from edges.
